question: For identical truth-conditional target proposition and explicit discourse context, how do Korean NOM-(n)un versus NOM-i/ka utterances differ in contextual felicity, contrast inference and perceived discourse continuity?

theoretical_competition.claim: The topic-versus-focus distinction predicts systematically higher -(n)un fit in continuing-about contexts and higher -i/ka fit in subject-answer contexts.
Discourse-reference salience rather than categorical focus marking predicts some -(n)un preference; sufficient contextual continuity may admit both variants.
Particle alone underdetermines focus; prosody, alternative set and reference-point discourse affect ratings.

source_policy: All 12 stimulus prompts and target sentences are newly authored fictional test materials. No outside learner corpus or archived PIA/hidden references. Separate lexical counterbalancing needed before population claims.

design.units: pair of same target clause and discourse-setting with particle alternation
design.target_meaning: neutral activity/state fact; context-specific alternative implicatures may change, must not be incorrectly called equivalent full pragmatic meaning
controls: identical nouns and verbs per pair
two syllable-final and nonfinal subject stems as balancing
preserve punctuation and written speech style
limits: One token replacement can alter information structure, presuppositions or contrast implications.
Written stimuli cannot identify spoken prosodic focus.
These contexts are small handcrafted examples, not a representative Korean population sample.
Do not fit participant effects until actual independent judgments exist.

stimuli.antecedent: 민지 이야기를 해 보자. 민지는 오늘 뭘 했어?
민지와 수아가 각각 무엇을 했는지 비교해 보자. 수아는 책을 읽었어. 민지는?
준혁의 근황을 이야기하자. 준혁은 오늘 무엇을 했어?
준혁과 영준의 일을 비교하자. 영준은 실험을 정리했어. 준혁은?

participant_tasks: Rate naturalness of continuation in this written context (1-7).
Rate whether utterance identifies a previously unresolved person (1-7).
Rate whether utterance suggests comparison with an unmentioned alternative (1-7).
Free-text alternate reading / discomfort; accept neither/both as genuine option.
measurement.primary_outcome: Within-context paired difference in naturalness ratings, topic minus nominative; report per-context first, no pooling until design expansion.
measurement.missingness: Never replace absent ratings with automatic model preference; no zero-cost abstentions.
measurement.analysis_if_data: Descriptive item-wise paired ratings; with participant sample use participant+lexical-item random effects and ordinal outcomes, predeclare model before data, no p-value from authored predictions.
measurement.blinding: Present two variants in counterbalanced left/right order, do not display context condition labels or H1/H2/H3.
measurement.pilot_first: Cognitive interview for context ambiguity and participant comprehension, then independently collected judgments. Pilot feedback may prompt a new version but never retroactively confirm this preseal.

stop_rule: No new proposer model, candidate generation budget or governor court required for this linguistic experiment. Only move to infrastructure if the target linguistic variable itself cannot be observed.
